name: Chris Harden
bio: Chris Harden is an attorney with more than 14 years of practice who is based in Woodstock, Georgia. He is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 11th Congressional District, which covers Bartow, Cherokee, Gordon, Pickens and part of Cobb counties.

platform.point: Cut taxes for the middle class while requiring large corporations and the wealthiest Americans to pay more.
Raise the federal minimum wage so full-time work covers a stable standard of living.
Protect Medicare and Medicaid, cap prescription drug costs and widen rural access to care.
Ban AI-driven surveillance pricing on essentials and act against corporate price gouging.
Expand clean energy, modernize the electric grid and keep Inflation Reduction Act tax credits.
Ban congressional stock trading, refuse corporate PAC money and impose a lifetime lobbying ban on former members.

economy.evidence: Calls for the wealthiest and large corporations to pay more, a higher minimum wage and action against price gouging.

welfare.evidence: Supports protecting Medicare and Medicaid, capping drug costs and expanding access to affordable care.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion, contraception and fertility-care access (choice) while being endorsed by gun-safety groups (regulation).

energy.evidence: Backs clean-energy expansion, grid modernization and keeping Inflation Reduction Act credits.

tech.evidence: Proposes banning AI surveillance pricing that uses personal data to set prices on essentials.

education.evidence: Prioritizes strong public schools plus career, technical and apprenticeship pathways.

name: Rick Allen
bio: Rick Allen has represented Georgia's 12th Congressional District in the U.S. House since 2015 and serves on the Education and the Workforce Committee. Before Congress he founded the Augusta construction firm R.W. Allen and Associates in 1976. He is from Augusta, Georgia.

platform.point: Supported the 2017 tax cuts and backs keeping taxes low for families and businesses.
Introduced legislation to limit environmental, social and governance (ESG) criteria in investing.
Supported freezing unspent Inflation Reduction Act funds.
Lists agriculture, economy and jobs, and education as his main legislative issue areas.

economy.evidence: Supported the 2017 tax cuts and sponsored bills restricting ESG investing rules.

welfare.evidence: Voted against the Mental Health Matters Act of 2022 and backed spending freezes.

liberty.evidence: Voted against the Respect for Marriage Act, cosponsored same-sex marriage bans and holds an F rating from NORML on cannabis.

immigration.evidence: Supported the 2017 executive order restricting entry from several Muslim-majority countries.

foreign.evidence: Initially backed Ukraine after the 2022 invasion but voted against a 2023 security assistance bill.

energy.evidence: Opposes ESG investing standards and supported freezing Inflation Reduction Act spending.

faith.evidence: Has cited Christian principles and Bible verses as the basis for positions on LGBT rights and Israel.

notes: No campaign website was confirmed; positions rest mainly on the Wikipedia summary of his record.

name: Ceretta Smith
bio: Ceretta Smith is a member of the Grovetown City Council. She served nearly a decade as a U.S. Army medic, then worked as a federal employee and labor leader, including as president of the AFGE Georgia State Council. She is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 12th Congressional District.

platform.point: Promote fair wages, good-paying jobs, job training and support for small businesses.
Expand coverage, lower out-of-pocket costs, strengthen rural clinics and add mental health services.
Fairly fund rural and low-income schools, raise educator pay and expand career pathways.
Improve transition support, cut red tape on benefits and expand veteran mental health care.
Address housing affordability and protect renters' rights.
Protect civil and reproductive rights, the freedom to organize and access to voting.

economy.evidence: Calls for fair wages, action on rising prices and protecting workers' freedom to organize.

welfare.evidence: Proposes expanding health coverage, lowering out-of-pocket costs and expanding mental health services.

liberty.evidence: Supports reproductive rights (choice) and common-sense gun safety measures with a Moms Demand Action endorsement (regulation).

education.evidence: Prioritizes fair funding for rural and low-income public schools and better educator pay.

name: Jasmine Clark
bio: Jasmine Clark has served in the Georgia House of Representatives for District 108 since 2019. She holds a PhD in microbiology from Emory University and has worked as a senior lecturer at Emory's nursing school. Born in Atlanta, she won the 2026 Democratic nomination for Georgia's 13th Congressional District after the death of Rep. David Scott.

platform.point: Require billionaires and corporations to pay their fair share, protect unions and help small businesses grow.
Expand health care access and restore reproductive health care rights.
Pass common-sense gun regulations, including an assault weapons ban.
Fully fund K-12 schools, protect HBCUs and lower child care costs.
Stop what she calls unconstitutional ICE raids.
Protect the climate, fight environmental racism and oppose data center overdevelopment.

economy.evidence: Wants billionaires and corporations to pay their fair share and supports union protections.

welfare.evidence: Calls for expanding health care access and lowering child care costs.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights and LGBTQ+ protections (choice) alongside an assault weapons ban (regulation).

security.evidence: Backs criminal justice reform and opposes ICE raids she calls unconstitutional.

immigration.evidence: Pledges to stop what she describes as unconstitutional ICE raids.

energy.evidence: Commits to climate protection and opposing environmental racism.

education.evidence: Supports fully funding K-12 public schools and opposes politicizing schools.

notes: The Commons portrait is a public-domain release credited to the Georgia House of Representatives, so it was not used under the photo rules.

name: Jonathan Chavez
bio: Jonathan Chavez is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 13th Congressional District. His campaign website describes him as a father of four and gives little other biographical detail.

platform.point: Replace the income tax with the FairTax, a national sales tax with household prebates, and abolish the IRS.
Repeal the Affordable Care Act in favor of market-based reforms with price transparency and pre-existing condition protections.
Expand school choice and charter options and reduce federal involvement in schools.
Increase resources for police and sheriff departments.
Pursue an America First policy of strong borders and a strong military.

economy.evidence: Backs the FairTax national sales tax, abolishing the IRS and deregulation.

welfare.evidence: Wants to repeal the ACA for market-driven care while keeping pre-existing condition protections.

security.evidence: Calls for more resources for police and sheriff departments.

immigration.evidence: Calls for secure, strong borders as part of an America First agenda.

foreign.evidence: Advocates peace through strength with a vigilant military under an America First approach.

energy.evidence: Emphasizes energy independence balanced with conservation of natural resources.

education.evidence: Champions school choice, more charter schools and parental control over education.

faith.evidence: Frames his campaign around Judeo-Christian values.

notes: Social media links on the campaign site were not functional, and no headshot separate from the logo was found.

name: Clay Fuller
bio: Clay Fuller has represented Georgia's 14th Congressional District since winning an April 2026 special election after Marjorie Taylor Greene resigned. He previously served as District Attorney for the Lookout Mountain Judicial Circuit from 2023 to 2026 and as a White House Fellow in 2018-2019. He is an Air Force judge advocate veteran and a lieutenant colonel in the Georgia Air National Guard.

platform.point: Support mass deportation of people in the country illegally, treating border security as national security.
Hold criminals accountable and fight fentanyl and drug trafficking.
Oppose restrictions on Second Amendment rights.
Advance an America First agenda to bring manufacturing jobs to northwest Georgia.

liberty.evidence: Opposes restrictions on gun rights under the Second Amendment.

security.evidence: As a prosecutor, emphasizes holding criminals accountable and combating drug trafficking.

immigration.evidence: Supports mass deportation of undocumented immigrants.

faith.evidence: Describes himself as a devout Christian and ties constitutional values to his faith.

notes: No official portrait flag in the input, so the Commons federal public-domain portrait is used; the campaign site image is a family photo, not a headshot.

name: Shawn Harris
current_role: Retired Army brigadier general and farmer
bio: Shawn Harris is a retired U.S. Army brigadier general and combat veteran who works as a farmer and small-business owner in northwest Georgia. He was the Democratic nominee against Marjorie Taylor Greene in 2024 and lost the April 2026 special election runoff to Clay Fuller.

platform.point: Expand Medicare to cover long-term nursing care, widen drug price negotiation and fund rural residency programs.
Oppose privatization and lift the payroll tax cap so high earners pay in all year.
Remove federal tax incentives and financing for institutional homebuyers and give individuals priority on foreclosures.
Suspend the federal gas tax temporarily and rebate a windfall tax on major oil companies to consumers.
Support the Second Amendment while requiring training and secure storage, and oppose arming teachers.
Support the Women's Health Protection Act to restore abortion access.

economy.evidence: Proposes lifting the payroll tax cap, a windfall tax on oil companies and required profit disclosures for large retailers.

welfare.evidence: Would expand Medicare to long-term nursing care and opposes vouchers and block grants for Medicare and Medicaid.

liberty.evidence: Backs the Women's Health Protection Act on abortion and strongly supports gun ownership, with training and safe-storage requirements.

tech.evidence: Proposes banning algorithmic surveillance pricing on groceries.

education.evidence: Supports restoring the U.S. Department of Education and federal support for public schools.

notes: Economy and tech scores were newly added from his cost-of-living issue page.

name: Andrew Underwood
bio: Andrew Underwood is the Libertarian nominee for Georgia's 14th Congressional District in 2026.
notes: No campaign website or public platform was found, and Ballotpedia could not be reached.

name: Ed Case
bio: Ed Case has represented Hawaii's 1st Congressional District since 2019 and previously represented the 2nd District from 2002 to 2007. He served in the Hawaii House from 1994 to 2002, including as majority leader, and practiced law for two decades. Born and raised in Hilo, he sits on the House Appropriations Committee.

platform.point: Prioritizes government reform and fiscal accountability in federal spending.
Co-chairs the Pacific Islands Caucus and focuses on national security in the Indo-Pacific.
Lists Hawaii's cost of living, small business and the economy among his priorities.
Focuses on environmental protection, wildfire recovery and the Red Hill fuel facility.
Lists Native Hawaiian issues and veterans' support as legislative priorities.

economy.evidence: A fiscally moderate former Blue Dog who joined eight Democrats resisting the 2021 $3.5 trillion budget package.

liberty.evidence: Rated 100% by NARAL on abortion, opposed same-sex marriage bans, and supports universal background checks for guns.

immigration.evidence: Rated 0% by immigration-reduction group FAIR, though he voted for the SAVE Act on voter citizenship proof.

foreign.evidence: Co-founded the Pacific Islands Caucus and voted to support Israel after the October 7 attacks.

energy.evidence: Rated 90% by the League of Conservation Voters and voted to keep the offshore drilling moratorium.

education.evidence: Rated 100% by the NEA and opposed school vouchers.

notes: Several OnTheIssues ratings and votes date from his 2002-2007 House tenure. No campaign website was confirmed.

name: Adriel Lam
bio: Adriel Lam is the Republican nominee for Hawaii's 1st Congressional District. His campaign emphasizes Hawaii's strategic role in the Pacific, and his website gives few other biographical details.

platform.point: End federal taxes on tips, overtime pay and Social Security benefits.
Reform the Jones Act to lower shipping costs for Hawaii.
Protect women's sports through policies on athlete eligibility.
Take a hard line on Iran and emphasize Hawaii's strategic Pacific role.

economy.evidence: Supports eliminating taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security and reforming the Jones Act.

liberty.evidence: Based only on his support for protecting women's sports on LGBTQ-related athlete eligibility.

foreign.evidence: Calls for a forceful approach to Iran and stresses Hawaii's strategic Pacific role.

notes: The liberty score rests on a single issue, and positions come mostly from social posts shown on his site.

name: Jordan Conley
bio: Jordan Conley is the Green Party nominee for Hawaii's 1st Congressional District in 2026.
notes: No campaign website or public platform was found, and Ballotpedia could not be reached.

name: Nathan Berning
bio: Nathan Berning is running as a nonpartisan candidate for Hawaii's 1st Congressional District in 2026.
notes: No campaign website or public platform was found, and Ballotpedia could not be reached.
